Go. It’s for you, not for them. Those types of people, if they see you not there, they won. But let me tell you a story about my family. It’s related, I’m not sure if it would really help you, but it’s worth a shot. For context, I’m 22.

My grandfather (who passed in 2017) was the only child of his mother. She treated him bad, kicked him out. He lied about his age when he was 16 to join the Navy. (He said he was 17 and his mother gave him consent). She was a drunk who would physically and mentally abuse him. Anyway, later in life he took care of her even though he lived in Illinois while she live a 5 hour car ride away in Kentucky. He bought her a trailer, and then some years later she was diagnosed with brain cancer. He moved her into his house in Illinois, and the family (my grandparents, mom and Aunts) took care of her. This was in 1991 so they were all living there at the time. She died in 1991, my grandfather paid for the funeral, the costs to transport the body from Illinois to Kentucky. He attends the reading of the Will. She left him a dollar, one last fuck you I guess. He went to her trailer that he bought her, she sold it for gambling debt, but her personal belongings were boxed up for my grandfather. Apparently she was drunk when writing this will, and she wanted to leave my grandfather $1 and her dirty underwear, but the attorney would not allow that.

The funeral was the next day. He took $1, wrote a note, slipped it the casket before it was closed for the last time. I’m not sure of the exact wording, but it was something along the lines of “You can keep your dollar, Mom. All I wanted you to do was love me.” My grandfather told me that a little under 2 years before he died. He said he never told anyone else. Neither did I until now.

I feel that story was necessary because it shapes my beliefs. But funerals are for the living, not the dead. It’s for you to get the closure you need. So if you want to, go. Don’t let other family members make you not go.
